requirements.title: Voice text and guided entry
requirements.requirement: Workers shall be able to speak, type or use structured questions for the same core workflow. Voice shall be optional; background listening shall be disabled. Users shall control recording, playback and deletion before submission.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A user completes each pilot journey without using a microphone and can review or correct a voice-derived value before confirmation.
requirements.current: Structured/text capture and gated on-device speech transcript review. Slices 2b and 3a: attached voice notes play back in the visit and can be deleted from drafts or discarded from the device queue. Slice 3d: voice notes recorded in the field notebook (24 kbps, up to 60 s) and queued offline. Slice 12a: a microphone on every text and number field of the workspace and the field notebook; one tap listens once, what was heard is reviewed and inserted only on request, and nothing is saved by speaking. On-device speech where the browser has it; the browser speech service only when an owner allows it in the synthetic or training environment.

requirements.title: Status that reflects reality

requirements.title: Patient matching with human resolution
requirements.requirement: The platform shall search permitted records using identifiers and selected demographics, present possible matches and support uncertain identities. A name or phone number alone shall not trigger an automatic merge.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Same-name, shared-phone, spelling-variant and twin cases remain distinct unless an authorised reviewer resolves the identity link.
requirements.current: R10 scoped exact/similar-name candidates, explicit separate/provisional decisions and clinician resolution. Slice 1c: merges need two different stewards and are never automatic; merged records are not offered as matches. Slice 10e: search by one complete issuer identifier (a linked ABHA number, RCH ID or Ni-kshay ID) inside the searcher's own care scope only; exact whole-value formats, so a partial or wildcard identifier is refused rather than searched; each search is a material read audited before it returns and a search that finds nothing is audited too; per-searcher limits (30 an hour, 8 finding nothing an hour, 24 a day); a record outside the scope gets the same answer as no record. The programme issuer formats are illustrative and unchecked against the registries. Atomic-review slice: D1 admission reservations bound concurrent ABHA review probes before lookup; stable retries do not probe again, generic refusal is preserved, and 32 local concurrent attempts admit exactly three. No raw ABHA or patient identifiers enter protection rows.
requirements.remaining: Issuer-registry-backed identifier lookup (nothing contacts an issuer), validated matching performance, timing and enumeration testing by an independent reviewer, and approved wider identity resolution.

The dry run lists the visits to create and the rows rejected with reasons, the SHA-256 of the file and a plan hash, and returns no clinical values or notes; apply takes only that plan and creates confirmed visits marked IMPORTED with lineage (file digest, row, importer, time) and no clinician review or sign-off implied, with a revision per visit and one counted audit event.
