Slice 6z: question ids that name Object.prototype members (constructor, toString and similar) are refused by the manifest schema, and answers and absence reasons are read as own properties only, for installed and compiled packs. Optional installed reviewed completion/referral declarations pin exact rule/question/version/hash and do not invent rules for legacy compiled packs.
requirements.remaining: Clinically approved pack content and a clinical sign-off workflow; new programme categories with MIS/EHR/report routing; automated schedules and escalation from installed rules; translations; per-team adoption; cross-organisation publication and production rollout.

requirements.title: Bounded task planning
requirements.requirement: The agent shall plan within an approved task catalogue and the user's current authority. It shall state what it can complete, what information is missing and which steps require human action.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An out-of-scope request receives a clear limitation or referral to the correct role and does not trigger an improvised external action.
requirements.current: Closed extraction/summary/review task catalogue and explicit unavailable states. Slice 6ab: the summary source lists text facts only (no entered-unit, unusual-reason or provenance objects).
requirements.remaining: Approved task catalogue and live-provider acceptance.

requirements.title: Context restricted to the task
requirements.requirement: The agent shall retrieve only the records and fields needed for the current purpose. Session memory shall be separated by tenant, person and encounter; patient details shall not become unrestricted global memory.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A cross-patient prompt cannot retrieve another person's information without a separately authorised task and permission check.
requirements.current: Patient/task-scoped input, exact-source approval and rejection of common identifiers in external narratives. Destination-specific structural/path allowlists and exact approved digest/mapping checks repeat at immediate transport for AI, frontline, image, MIS, EHR/ABDM, aggregate and mock enrolment. Decoded-source Unicode/contact guards and unrelated known narrative checks preserve approved body/hash rather than silently rewriting it.
requirements.remaining: Representative sensitive-data leak evaluation across real profiles and purpose-specific review; provider agreements/retention and wider unmapped destination contracts remain external or incomplete.

requirements.title: Eligibility before tool selection
requirements.requirement: Tool selection shall first apply jurisdiction, role, intended use, population, input quality, evidence status, consent or other authorisation, language and connectivity constraints. Cost and speed can rank only eligible tools.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A cheaper or available tool with an incompatible approved use is never substituted into the workflow.
requirements.current: Use-time checks for reviewed capability, model/agent, age, care team/role, task, language, setting and browser device.
requirements.remaining: Jurisdiction, broader population/clinical scope, professional verification and quality eligibility acceptance.

requirements.title: Approved execution paths
requirements.requirement: The agent shall use a defined tool catalogue with validated inputs and outputs. Retrieved text, documents and model responses shall be treated as content, not as authority to grant access or change execution policy.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Instructions embedded in a patient note or provider output cannot activate a new tool, reveal credentials or bypass a confirmation.
requirements.current: Closed command/output schemas and grounded proposals cannot grant tools or credentials.
requirements.remaining: Independent adversarial review and live-provider corpus acceptance.

requirements.title: Human authority at action boundaries
requirements.requirement: The platform shall distinguish draft preparation, routine authorised recording and consequential clinical or external actions. Actions shall require the confirmation and professional authority defined in Section 21.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: The agent cannot make itself the approving actor, and expired approvals cannot be reused for changed data or a different destination.
requirements.current: Actor-bound explicit approvals expire and stale data invalidates them.
requirements.remaining: Clinical authority policy and independently accepted action-boundary scenarios.

requirements.title: Durable progress and recovery
requirements.requirement: The agent shall retain the state of each step, its outcome and dependencies so an interrupted task can resume without duplicating completed external actions.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A failure after one destination accepts a record does not repeat that submission; the user sees and can recover only unfinished steps.
requirements.current: Durable running checkpoints, receipts and no automatic repeat after ambiguous completion.
requirements.remaining: Full multi-step dependency recovery with real destinations and operational owners.

requirements.title: Limits and cancellation
requirements.requirement: Every task shall have limits on time, tool calls, retries and spend. Users shall be able to stop pending activity. Cancelling cannot falsely reverse an action already accepted elsewhere.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A looping provider interaction stops at the configured limit and reports which actions completed, were cancelled or remain unresolved.
requirements.current: One-call checkpointing, timeout/cancellation, per-capability daily call and reserved-token quotas; no automatic provider substitution. Slice 5a: monthly USD budgets per capability (estimates from recorded rates) checked before preparing and before sending; clinicians and supervisors with care scope can stop another worker's unsent request; sent requests are never reported as recalled. Slice 5e: per-capability task time and attempt limits in the reviewed manifest; unsent requests expire at the limit; a sent request without a result past the limit is shown as timed out with an uncertain outcome, never retried, and closed only by a recorded human decision; attempts beyond the limit refused before preparing and before sending; owner-owned budget alerts at 80% and 100% of estimated use. Slice 5h: owners record a provider invoice summary per provider and month and reconcile it against Saha's recorded estimates per model, with an owner-set threshold flag; records are append-only and audited, later ones supersede earlier ones, and budgets and rates are never changed automatically; owner-owned alerts for flagged variance and providers used without a reconciliation in the previous month.
requirements.remaining: A looping-provider stop reporting completed/cancelled/unresolved actions across multi-step tasks, background detection and delivery of timed-out requests, provider billing API reconciliation, delivered alerts and validated provider outage operation.

requirements.title: Conflicting outputs
requirements.requirement: Contradictory or incomparable model outputs shall be shown as such and routed according to approved policy. The agent shall not average risk scores, invent a consensus or suppress a qualifying warning unless a validated composition explicitly permits it.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A designed model-disagreement case produces a review task with both original outputs and no fabricated combined diagnosis.
requirements.current: Conflicting extraction candidates are withheld; original results remain separate. Slice 5c: values that conflict with recorded facts or another open result are flagged on both results, listed as one action-plan review task with every original value, never combined, and applied only after an explicit choice with a reason.
requirements.remaining: Cross-model composition policy, routing beyond the requesting worker, comparison with earlier confirmed records and validated disagreement handling for risk outputs.

requirements.title: Evidence behind explanations
requirements.requirement: Explanations shall identify the relevant recorded facts, protocol or model and any material uncertainty. They shall not claim certainty from model confidence or supply unsupported clinical advice.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Reviewers can trace each consequential recommendation to its underlying rule or approved output; unsupported answers are withheld or escalated.
requirements.current: Exact field evidence plus saved protocol findings with source edition/link and service-version attribution. Protocols can retain exact acquired document digest alongside edition/link. All acquired dependencies are checked for integrity, source scope and expiry before review/activation; normal expiry and deliberate-corruption defensive tests are distinct.
requirements.remaining: Verified/licensed clinical source content and consequential recommendation acceptance on representative scenarios.

requirements.title: Clinical workflow continuity without an LLM
requirements.requirement: Loss of the language model shall not prevent structured capture, access to valid cached protocols, a local draft referral or visibility of urgent tasks. The interface shall make unavailable functions explicit.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A simulated LLM outage leaves the core non-generative encounter workflow usable without substituting invented AI results.
requirements.current: Structured capture and current source-backed rule/referral review operate without a model. A05 adds signed prepared documentary task types and complete captured programme pack/version guidance, encrypted offline conditional answers and explicit absence reasons. New server-held work digests and captured episode/version checks apply before sync even if an older client omits its optional digest. Sync remains an unconfirmed draft; clinical approval remains pending.
requirements.remaining: Approved outage pathways, offline cached protocols and device-level escalation acceptance.

requirements.title: Programme manager analysis
requirements.requirement: Authorised managers may request questions over approved datasets and metric definitions. The agent shall disclose the cohort, time period, data freshness, filters and method, and enforce the same restrictions as standard reporting.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A natural-language count matches the governed report and cannot expose restricted patient lists through a reformulated query.
requirements.current: Slice 6d: a catalogue of eight versioned indicators queried over the viewer's scope with cohort minimum, small-cell and complementary suppression and freshness, plus a keyword interpreter that maps a question to catalogue entries for review without running it or using a model. Slice 6s: the catalogue is an owner-maintained registry of versioned definitions built from a fixed vocabulary of measures, filters and exclusions; the interpreter follows the registry; results name their definition version; one viewer's nested queries over seven days are checked for differencing and withheld when they would reveal a group of 1 to 4 people. Slice 6w: indicator queries are POST only (GET answers the catalogue and interpretation), a view no longer commits organisation-wide, and the CSV export is recorded as an access-audit event; differencing fixes as in BR-REP-04. Slice 6aa: indicator results carry the stated limits of small-group protection, and owners see them in the registry; the population-based differencing check withholds more results for small teams and narrow filters.
requirements.remaining: Natural-language analysis under governance, validated definitions with an approval workflow, owner-defined measures, and differencing protection across viewers, non-nested filters and groupings.

requirements.title: Change control for the agent
requirements.requirement: Material changes to prompts, tool descriptions, routing rules, model versions and knowledge sources shall be versioned and tested against the release suite. Production learning from user interactions shall not silently change behaviour.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Operators can identify the exact configuration behind an encounter and restore a previously approved configuration after a regression.
requirements.current: Pinned agent/model and immutable capability revisions; independent review, retirement/hold and scoped related-encounter list.
requirements.remaining: Formal prompt/routing change approval, complete impact analysis and operational rollback validation.

requirements.title: Capability registration
requirements.requirement: Every capability shall have an accountable provider, a stable identity, version, purpose, input and output definitions, deployment scope, evidence, operating limits and a support contact. Clinical and administrative capabilities shall be clearly distinguished.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Registration cannot reach an active state while mandatory manifest fields or accountable ownership are missing.
requirements.current: Versioned capability manifest records owner, model/task/context scope, support and data terms; reviewed activation required. Independent anaemia demo: separate provider organisation, customer agreement revision and independent administration; demo agreement only. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Live provider onboarding, evidence ownership and verification of the full accountable manifest.

requirements.title: Intended use and excluded use
requirements.requirement: Each capability shall specify authorised users, populations, age range where relevant, settings, languages, devices, required input quality and excluded uses. Eligibility shall be machine-checkable where possible and explicitly reviewable elsewhere.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A capability approved for adults cannot run on a child case unless that use has separate approval.
requirements.current: Documentary capabilities enforce age, role/team, language, setting, device and task scope; clinical generation remains unavailable. Independent anaemia demo: explicitly synthetic environment and patient, normal care-role/team scope and per-image synthetic approval. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Verified intended use, jurisdiction and broader population criteria with representative clinical evidence.

requirements.title: Evidence and deployment authorisation
requirements.requirement: Evidence records shall identify model version, evaluation context, limitations and review decisions. Regulatory status and local deployment authorisation shall be recorded separately from technical integration and sandbox evaluation.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A technically successful API test cannot activate a clinical capability without the required documented evidence and deployment approvals.
requirements.current: Version-bound synthetic evaluation, separate clinical review and owner activation are persisted and checked at use. Independent anaemia demo remains outside clinical activation and carries clinicalUse:false; real model use is engineering-only.
requirements.remaining: Regulatory status, representative clinical evidence and signed deployment authorisation; no real approval recorded.

requirements.title: Capability lifecycle
requirements.requirement: The lifecycle shall cover registered, technically verified, under review, approved for a scope, active, suspended, retired and replaced. Activation shall be deployment-specific and allow trial or shadow status without exposing unapproved results to care.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A provider cannot self-activate; suspension blocks new invocations and identifies in-progress work requiring cancellation or review.
requirements.current: Draft/reviewed/active/suspended/retired revisions, replacement history and scoped affected-encounter views. Slice 5d: BRD lifecycle stages derived per package (registered, technically verified, approved for scope, active, suspended, retired, replaced), replacement recorded on activation, use counted per exact version, and in-progress work of an unusable capability identified with its required action (cancel, withheld, review, check applied values) on the governance page and in the audit line. Slice 5f: shadow operation of a reviewed revision for named teams or the whole organisation over at most 30 days; runs on confirmed visits (local rules provider only) without showing, applying or planning its output; consent, restriction, budget and lifecycle respected. Slice 6q (second independent review): a shadow's teams are limited to the revision's reviewed teams (organisation scope is the overlap); running and stopping need an owner or a member of every shadow team, also on replay; visits outside the runner's normal care scope are skipped and counted.
requirements.remaining: Verified registration step, deployment-specific activation, automatic and live-provider shadow runs, delivered impact queues and live lifecycle acceptance.

requirements.title: Contract validation
requirements.requirement: Adapters shall validate required inputs, accepted types, ranges, units, response states and result semantics. Binary media requirements and large or asynchronous responses shall be documented.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Malformed or unsupported responses are quarantined with an actionable error and cannot be presented as a valid clinical result.
requirements.current: Strict documentary output contracts, exact evidence/field checks and checkpointed failed results. Independent anaemia demo: strict versioned image/result contract, HMAC and input binding, one-call durable checkpoint and receipt-only recovery. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Capability-specific clinical semantics, media/asynchronous contracts and governed rejected-response quarantine.

requirements.title: Input quality and inability to assess
requirements.requirement: The workflow shall check signal quality and record insufficient-input, unsupported-case, unavailable and unable-to-assess states separately from a low-risk or negative result.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A noisy cough recording produces a quality failure or valid retry instruction, never an implied negative screen.
requirements.current: Invalid/unavailable results stay separate; extraction uncertainty is withheld and language gates fail independently. Slice 5c: an explicit unable-to-assess outcome (noisy input, unsupported case, insufficient input) with a retry instruction and no values, shown as such and never applied. Independent anaemia demo: technical-quality unable_to_assess has no score; unknown outcomes remain unresolved without inference retry.
requirements.remaining: Signal/media quality checks, per-field assessment, complete unsupported-population taxonomy and representative validation.

requirements.title: Version pinning
requirements.requirement: Production invocations shall bind to an approved provider and model version or an equivalently controlled provider release identifier. Undisclosed provider updates shall be treated as contract violations requiring review.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A provider version change triggers quarantine or controlled reapproval and cannot silently replace a validated version.
requirements.current: Agent/model/capability/corpus versions are bound; legacy HTTP AI bypass is disabled. Slice 5g: provider and model history per capability key (pinned provider, model and agent version per revision, changes from the previous revision, activity period, stage and request counts) for governance managers. Independent anaemia demo: pinned provider, ONNX model/hash and contract retained per request. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Formal provider change review, live contract compatibility and historical legacy provenance limitations.

requirements.title: Least-data provider invocation
requirements.requirement: Each call shall include only the fields and media needed for the approved purpose. Provider retention, training use, subprocessors and hosting region shall be recorded and compatible with the deployment agreement.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Payload inspection confirms excluded identifiers are absent and a provider with incompatible retention terms is blocked.
requirements.current: Structured identity excluded; common free-text identifiers rejected; manifest retains region, retention, training prohibition and agreement reference. Independent anaemia demo: cropped RGB only, no identity/notes/EXIF, no stored image pixels in either request ledger. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval. Mapped AI/frontline narratives are checked after decoding; normalization is used only for comparison, retaining the exact approved wire body/hash. Cropped image envelopes require exact RGB dimensions/digest and exclude identity/EXIF. Independent destination/header review retains the original defensive findings and verifies repaired transport boundaries.
requirements.remaining: Complete representative minimisation assessment and enforceable provider retention, training, subprocessor and region compliance; no clinical or real-provider acceptance.

requirements.title: Multi-provider result history
requirements.requirement: The platform shall retain provider attribution and original output for each invocation. Replacing a provider shall not overwrite historical results or obscure the version used for an earlier decision.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An encounter spanning a provider change shows both results independently with their input timestamps and review states.
requirements.current: Original outputs, model/provider, versioned source and reasoned human decisions are retained. Independent anaemia demo: saved signed result, consent/visit/agreement versions and reasoned staff acknowledgement or rejection; no automatic clinical record update. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Complete legacy provenance, end-to-end input-time semantics and external-provider acceptance.

requirements.title: Monitoring and safety suspension
requirements.requirement: Monitoring shall cover availability, latency, input-quality failures, unsupported cases, usage, incidents and reviewed outcome measures where suitable ground truth exists. Clinical degradation shall trigger the approved investigation and suspension process.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Operators can suspend a named version, identify affected encounters and assign follow-up without disabling unrelated safe capabilities.
requirements.current: Versioned fixture scores by field/language/group, scoped related records, safety cases and immediate capability hold. Slice 5f: shadow outputs compared per field with clinician-confirmed values (agreement, disagreement, missing, not recorded, unable to assess), counts only to governance managers. Slice 5i: drift monitoring per capability revision from shadow comparisons: agreement rate per 7-day period by visit confirmation date over the last four periods, and a flag when the rate drops by more than 10 percentage points between consecutive periods with at least 10 rated fields each, counts only, to governance managers on the Clinical governance page; nothing is suspended automatically. Slice 6q: shadow comparisons (the drift input) no longer include teams outside the revision's reviewed teams or patients outside the runner's care scope. Slice 13c: shadow and drift counts use the comparison as it stands now: recomputed against a confirmed correction, left out for a voided visit or an unconfirmed correction.
requirements.remaining: Representative quality monitoring on live, representative data rather than local-rules shadow comparisons, configurable drift thresholds, drift from synthetic evaluations, independent ground-truth annotation and adjudication, delivered alerting and clinical response operations.

requirements.title: Provider self-service in a controlled environment
requirements.requirement: Providers may maintain documentation, credentials for testing and proposed versions in an isolated environment using approved synthetic data. They shall not publish directly to production or inspect unrestricted patient payloads.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Provider test access remains limited to its own capability and synthetic environment; production activation follows the standard review path.
requirements.current: Slice 5b: provider sandbox organisations (no patient records, one provider) with a provider-only role limited to its own documentation, credential references, capability proposals and synthetic evaluations; owner import into production as a draft that must pass production evaluation, independent review and owner activation. Slice 6p (independent review): the sandbox import no longer reads another organisation before checking ownership, and gives one 404 for not found, not a sandbox and not the importer's own. Eight frontline demo providers: independent apps/stores, speech or printed-text OCR, confirmed synthetic input, checkpointed signed receipts and staff review; no clinical deployment approval.
requirements.remaining: Physically isolated environment, provider-registered test endpoints, provider-facing contract and independent acceptance.

requirements.title: Cost and contractual limits
requirements.requirement: Usage shall be metered by provider, capability, deployment and task, with budget limits and alerts. Financial incentives shall not override clinical eligibility or conceal a recommended provider substitution.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Reaching a cost limit results in a visible controlled fallback and does not silently select an unapproved model.
requirements.current: Per-capability daily call and reserved-token limits with reported usage and bounded synthetic evaluations. Slice 5a: owner-set monthly USD budget per capability, estimated from recorded rates and reservations, refusal with a visible message and no provider substitution, and budget use on the Operations page. Slice 5e: computed alerts at 80% and 100% of a capability's estimated monthly budget, owned and acknowledged by organisation owners, labelled as estimates; per-capability task attempt limits. Slice 5h: invoice reconciliation per provider, model and month (Saha's estimated tokens and USD against owner-recorded invoiced tokens and USD, with differences and an owner-set threshold flag), append-only and audited with supersession, shown to owners and administrators on Operations, and owner-owned variance and unreconciled-month alerts.
requirements.remaining: Provider and deployment budgets, delivered (pushed) budget alerts, evaluation and other AI cost coverage, reconciliation by provider billing API rather than an owner-entered summary, and per-provider or historical cost rates.

requirements.title: Approved source library
requirements.requirement: Clinical content shall come from approved, versioned sources with publisher, effective date, local applicability and reviewer. Retrieval shall favour content approved for the current programme and user role.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Superseded or unapproved guidance cannot be offered as current advice, and each displayed recommendation links to its source.
requirements.current: Immutable source metadata retains publisher/edition/link, applicability, owner, effective dates and independent review; protocols cite it. Immutable acquired source bytes now support bounded UTF-8/PDF upload, exact digest-pinned scoped download and default-off allowlisted HTTPS retrieval with size/expiry/redirect limits. Independent clinician review and activation remain separate; acquired dependencies must retain exact integrity/scope/expiry before activation.
requirements.remaining: Licensed approved clinical content acquisition, publisher/owner verification, clinical authorisation and representative recommendation acceptance; synthetic document transport does not approve content.

requirements.title: Controlled clinical logic
requirements.requirement: Eligibility, warning signs, thresholds, contraindications and referral logic shall be represented through approved rules or explicitly approved clinical capabilities. The language model may explain them but may not rewrite them during a visit.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Rephrasing a prompt does not change a protocol's decision for the same confirmed facts.
requirements.current: Bounded declarative observation/worker-concern rules with age/programme scope, freshness, sources and verified service dependencies.
requirements.remaining: Clinically approved eligibility/red-flag logic, contraindications/interactions and scenario acceptance.

requirements.title: Escalation without model dependence
requirements.requirement: When an approved protocol identifies a need for urgent escalation, the application shall show the locally approved action and contacts immediately. A pending AI call shall not delay that action.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An urgent synthetic scenario follows the configured escalation path when cloud AI and external MIS services are unavailable.
requirements.current: Model-independent urgent-review findings cite current sources and service contacts; unknowns remain explicit.
requirements.remaining: Approved escalation pathways, response operations and verified offline clinical availability.

requirements.title: Scope of practice
requirements.requirement: Advice and available actions shall reflect the user's verified authority. A worker may record observations and prepare referrals only within the approved scope; medical decisions requiring a clinician shall be routed accordingly.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: User role changes modify available clinical actions, and server-side tests reject unauthorised orders.
requirements.current: Role checks prevent supervisor clinical writes; prescribing/ordering is unavailable.
requirements.remaining: Verified professional authority and action-specific clinical scope policies.

requirements.title: Review and override
requirements.requirement: An authorised reviewer shall be able to accept, reject or override a suggestion with a reason. Overrides shall preserve the original evidence and shall feed quality review without automatically retraining a model.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: The record distinguishes the model recommendation from the human decision and identifies the responsible professional.
requirements.current: Reasoned accept/reject/override decisions retain original assistant and protocol evidence; clinician-only protocol decisions.
requirements.remaining: Verified clinical authority and acceptance across all consequential task types and corrections.

requirements.title: Model-specific quality requirements
requirements.requirement: Each clinical capability shall have a separate acceptance plan appropriate to its task, population and intended use, including relevant subgroup performance and uncertainty. There shall be no generic platform-wide clinical accuracy percentage.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Clinical activation requires a signed capability-specific evidence review; administrative usability results cannot substitute for clinical validation.
requirements.current: No signed task/population-specific clinical acceptance evidence.
requirements.remaining: Capability-specific study plan, subgroup review, uncertainty and signed authorisation.

requirements.title: Composition safety
requirements.requirement: When several tools feed a single recommendation, the combined workflow shall be evaluated for interactions, missing inputs and disagreement. Individual model approvals shall not be treated as approval of every possible combination.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: The activated workflow has a reviewed composition and tested conflict scenarios; unapproved combinations are unavailable.
requirements.current: No clinical composition is enabled.
requirements.remaining: Validated compositions and disagreement/missing-input safety evaluations before enabling them.

requirements.title: Harm reporting and review
requirements.requirement: Users shall be able to flag misleading advice, wrong-patient results, missed escalation and potential harm from the current encounter. Reports shall reach a named clinical owner with evidence and action tracking.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A safety report creates a visible case, preserves relevant versions and can initiate a capability hold and affected-case review.
requirements.current: Encounter-linked safety cases bind original versions, named clinical ownership, resolution evidence and optional capability/protocol hold.
requirements.remaining: Real incident response operations, independent review and harm reporting acceptance.

requirements.title: Integration readiness contract
requirements.requirement: Each connector shall record the system owner, permitted read and write operations, identity method, data contract, authorisation, test environment, support contact and operational limits. Unknown capabilities shall remain explicitly unverified.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A connector cannot be labelled live until the receiving owner has accepted its tested scope and production access is enabled.
requirements.current: MIS/EHR configuration, capability probes and scoped credential gates.
requirements.remaining: Receiving-owner contracts, complete supported operations and live acceptance.

requirements.title: Independent read and write permissions
requirements.requirement: Read access, creation, update, deletion, status lookup and aggregation shall be separately configurable. Permission to retrieve a record shall not imply permission to modify it or register a patient.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A read-only connector exposes no active write path and clearly states when programme updates require a separate process.
requirements.current: EHR read/write directions and local scoped permissions are independent. Slice 7e: every programme destination, EHR connection and the mock ABDM gateway has owner-managed, versioned and audited create, update, delete or void, lookup and aggregate permissions, checked on the server before preparation and again inside each external-execution checkpoint; a withdrawal closes the item as not sent, shown on the trace and in the exception queue. Slice 6ab: a correction to a demonstration destination is classified as update by an accepted submission of a visit it corrects; ABDM consent requests are governed by lookup (a revocation always applies; delete decides only whether the mock gateway is told); an EHR publication rechecks create before its Patient read.
requirements.remaining: Live partner adapters configured and tested with narrowed operations; void and aggregate report paths; AI providers are not covered; production acceptance.

requirements.title: Confirmed submission receipts
requirements.requirement: Every attempted external write shall retain destination, submitted version, time, initiating authority, status and receipt or error. Acceptance shall require the destination's meaningful acknowledgement, not merely a successful HTTP transport response.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A response containing a business rejection is shown as rejected even when the network request technically succeeded.
requirements.current: Outbox and meaningful business receipts/errors are retained per destination.
requirements.remaining: Actual partner acceptance and authorisation evidence.

requirements.title: Duplicate prevention and uncertain outcomes
requirements.requirement: Retries shall use stable submission identity and destination-supported duplicate controls. Where acceptance is uncertain, the platform shall reconcile before resubmitting or route the case for review.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A timeout after external acceptance does not create a second patient or activity; an unverifiable outcome remains visibly unresolved.
requirements.current: Stable keys, lookup-before-resend and uncertain outcomes tested with mock transport. Slice 6u: an EHR publication refused before its write request (patient check or authority recheck) is closed as not sent ('blocked') instead of staying uncertain; one that may have been sent stays uncertain and needs a receipt lookup. Slice 7f: an owner may declare per EHR connection, from the partner contract, that its identifier search is authoritative with a consistency delay; an uncertain publication then resolves by lookup as accepted (one equal match), not stored after the delay (closed, never resent; a new publication only through the normal approval) or conflict (several or a different match); default off keeps the earlier rule. Each lookup checks its operation, is audited before sending, traced and limited to 24 per publication; the write must start within 30 s of the checkpoint. Replay soak: unresolved EHR share about 21% for the default partner and 0 for the authoritative one, no duplicate stored document.
requirements.remaining: Real partner duplicate/reconciliation contracts and timeout acceptance; partner evidence that its search is authoritative and its consistency delay holds.

requirements.title: Partial completion across systems
requirements.requirement: The platform shall track each destination independently and support recovery from partial success. It shall not promise an atomic transaction across unrelated MIS systems or automatically delete valid records to simulate rollback.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: If one of two writes succeeds, the success receipt is preserved and only the failed or uncertain destination is retried.
requirements.current: Independent destination states preserve accepted receipts during partial failure.
requirements.remaining: Two live systems demonstrate the same recovery behaviour.

requirements.title: Inbound changes and reconciliation
requirements.requirement: Approved inbound updates shall identify source, version and effective time. Conflicts with local work shall enter a review process, and outstanding receipts shall be reconciled on a schedule appropriate to the connector.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An external status change does not silently discard an unsynchronised local correction, and the responsible reviewer sees both.
requirements.current: Receipt callbacks/lookups and staged document imports preserve source data. Slice 6u: programme callbacks are authenticated (server grant and signature) before any organisation data is read, and every authentication failure gets the same 401. Reviewed retrieval handoff and current-service repair retain original records/receipts and refuse revocation during the final response; exact saved history receipt replay performs no external retry or new care write.
requirements.remaining: Scheduled reconciliation and broader inbound clinical conflict queues.

requirements.title: Schema and mapping change control
requirements.requirement: External form, code or API changes shall trigger compatibility checks and owner review. Failed validation shall pause affected submissions while preserving queued data and unaffected workflows.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A removed mandatory destination field causes a controlled connector exception, not silent data loss or guessed replacement values.
requirements.current: Connector versions invalidate queued approvals; mapping fixtures reject unsupported fields.
requirements.remaining: Owner-reviewed external schema change detection and preserved-queue migration.

requirements.title: Limited integration alternatives
requirements.requirement: Where approved APIs are unavailable, owner-authorised file exchange or assisted submission may be supported and labelled as such. Credentials, access controls or usage restrictions shall not be bypassed to simulate connectivity.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Exported files carry reconciliation identifiers; a prepared export is never reported as accepted until acceptance evidence is recorded.
requirements.current: Labelled FHIR document import/export without assumed acceptance.
requirements.remaining: Owner-authorised batch/assisted workflows with reconciliation identifiers and receipts.

requirements.title: Per-destination data minimisation
requirements.requirement: Each connector shall send only authorised fields needed by its contract. Person-level operational data shall not be sent to an aggregate-reporting system merely because both are labelled health MIS.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Payload fixtures and production audits verify field allowlists and distinguish person records from aggregate measures.
requirements.current: Per-destination mapped field allowlists. Slice 7e: aggregate-only programme destinations refuse every patient-level record before preparation and inside the delivery checkpoint. Slice 7g: an aggregate-only demonstration destination receives approved aggregate reports only: suppressed cells from named indicator versions, a definition and version manifest, row count and SHA-256; a payload minimisation check (no patient-level field or identifier value, no released cell from 1 to 4) runs before preparing, before the checkpoint and inside it, and its result is recorded on the report; a failed check closes the report as not sent. Slice 6ab: aggregate report screening also uses the slice 6aa population check (preparation, pre-send recomputation and checkpoint), and a ledger write D1 refuses closes the report as not sent. Slice 6ad (ninth review): aggregate report reads return the manifest and withheld blocks but never the cells (figures go to the destination only); payloads are kept only while a report is open and bounded (150 kB each, 450 kB for all reports beside the 1 MB ledger); only open reports count towards the limit of 20 and unapproved or unsent reports expire after 24 hours; a late destination answer is appended as evidence; receipt lookup stays available in maintenance and the send checkpoint re-checks maintenance. Patient-level destination envelopes now constrain paths/fields/current mapping and exact approved digest, and repeat sensitive checks before immediate send. Aggregate malformed arrays fail closed and suppression repeats even for a rehashed stored body. Validated FHIR headers are materialised without losing conditional-create fields; server credentials are added last, caller credentials refused, uncertain lookup remains body-free.
requirements.remaining: Live destination contracts, representative real-profile minimisation and partner testing; synthetic boundary evidence does not complete all destination-specific semantics.

requirements.title: Standards-based exchange
requirements.requirement: Where an ecosystem requires a published standard or implementation guide, the connector shall use a pinned agreed version and pass its conformance checks. ABDM exchange shall follow the applicable onboarding flows and the current agreed ABDM FHIR profiles [S1, S2, S8, S9].
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Standards validation and owner acceptance are recorded separately; valid FHIR content alone does not mark the connector production-ready.
requirements.current: Native FHIR R4 subset with explicit conformance limitations.
requirements.remaining: Pinned ecosystem implementation guides, validators and independent owner acceptance.

requirements.title: Canonical exchange representation
requirements.requirement: The platform shall maintain a canonical representation for person, encounter, observation, condition, service request, care plan, medication, diagnostic result, document and provenance. Source payloads and destination payloads shall remain traceable to this representation without erasing material differences.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A single confirmed blood-pressure observation can be mapped to two approved destinations, and the audit shows the original source, canonical value, units, mapping version and each destination payload.
requirements.current: Person/visit/observations and document Bundle mapping.
requirements.remaining: Canonical condition, service request, medication, diagnostic result and full provenance semantics.

requirements.title: Source and destination provenance
requirements.requirement: Every imported or exported clinical element shall retain source system, source identifier, author or device where known, effective time, receipt time, transformation version and confidence or verification state. A transformed record shall not be represented as if the platform originally measured it.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An imported laboratory result and an ASHA-recorded observation remain distinguishable after display, export and reconciliation.
requirements.current: Imported source documents, timestamps and local submission provenance retained.
requirements.remaining: Element-level author/device, receipt/effective time and transformation lineage for all resources.

requirements.title: ABDM participation scope
requirements.requirement: Each deployment shall explicitly approve the ABDM modules and roles it uses, including any ABHA, Scan and Share, HIP, HIU, consented exchange or NHCX capability. Permission for one module or role shall not imply another.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Administration and test evidence identify the enabled ABDM role, environment, facility, client credentials, approved operations and responsible owner; all other operations are unavailable.
requirements.current: Slice 7a: owner-recorded ABDM environment (mock only), ABHA/HIP/HIU modules, facility identifier and an approval reference per module; ABHA and HIU actions refused unless their module is enabled with approval. Local mock gateway only.
requirements.remaining: Sandbox and production onboarding, real credentials, facility registry verification and deployment-specific enforcement.

requirements.title: ABHA identity and record linking
requirements.requirement: ABHA creation, verification, demographic matching and record linking shall use authorised flows and explicit user confirmation where required. The platform shall support care for a person without ABHA when the approved workflow permits and shall not merge people solely because names, phones or demographic fields are similar.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Tests cover verified ABHA linkage, declined linkage, absent ABHA, duplicate candidates, demographic mismatch and later correction without wrong-person disclosure.
requirements.current: Slice 7a: ABHA link after a mock one-time-code check, decline, unlink with history and consent revocation, one current record per ABHA number, masked display. Local mock gateway only. Slice 6r: patient history is redacted on read (ABHA numbers masked in revision data and field changes, received bundles withheld); stored revisions unchanged. Slice 6u: when the record already holding an ABHA number is outside the worker's scope, the link refusal is neutral and does not reveal it. Slice 6z: that refusal is now the ordinary link refusal (same status and text as a gateway refusal), and the server records the conflict as an audit event on the holding record for an identity steward; the requester is not told. Slice 6ab: an ABHA held by an out-of-scope record is refused before the one-time code is looked at; because the mock code is public the refusal is still distinguishable from a link, so the oracle is bounded (one steward review event per requester and holding record a day; after three in a day every further link by that requester is refused the same way), not removed. Slice 10e: an ABHA number is accepted as 14 digits or grouped 2-4-4-4 with hyphens and refused otherwise, in the link command and in search. No checksum is applied because no official specification of one was found: the PIB explainer and community guides call it a random 14-digit number, and abdm.gov.in and the sandbox documents could not be read from the build environment. ABHA review reservations apply before linking lookups, including audit-failure retention and rollout coverage; no live ABDM acceptance is implied.
requirements.remaining: Authorised ABHA creation and verification with ABDM, a checksum if ABDM specifies one, issuer checks, and correction through ABDM.

requirements.title: ABDM consent enforcement
requirements.requirement: For ABDM exchanges that require a consent artefact, the platform shall enforce the named HIU and HIP, purpose, health information types, date range, expiry and status. Revocation, expiry or mismatch shall stop new retrieval or disclosure and create an auditable outcome.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Requests outside the approved purpose, date range, data type or validity period are blocked even when the calling user can otherwise view the local patient record.
requirements.current: Slice 7a: consent artefacts with purpose, health-information types, record date range, expiry and revocation; fetch checks enforce status, ABHA link, purpose, type and date. The consent manager is simulated by an owner; local mock gateway only.
requirements.remaining: Real consent-manager integration, HIP/HIU callbacks, notifications and enforcement on actual ABDM exchange.

requirements.title: Facility and professional attribution
requirements.requirement: Where the ABDM or EHR workflow requires organisation, facility or practitioner attribution, the platform shall use verified HFR, HPR or destination identifiers and the active role. It shall not invent identifiers or reuse a professional identity across an unapproved facility context.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A consultation bundle fails validation or enters review when the configured facility or practitioner attribution is absent, expired or inconsistent with the encounter.
requirements.current: Document publisher and patient link configuration exist.
requirements.remaining: Verified HFR/HPR or destination professional/facility attribution and expiry checks.

requirements.title: ABDM FHIR conformance and version control
requirements.requirement: ABDM clinical artefacts shall conform to the pinned NRCeS FHIR implementation package agreed for the deployment. The validator, profile set, terminology content and mapping shall be versioned together; upgrades require regression testing and owner approval [S2].
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Every outbound test bundle passes the pinned validator; a deliberate profile violation is rejected with a specific error and no external submission.
requirements.current: Slice 7c: a pinned, versioned structural rule set (FHIR R4 Bundle invariants bdl-7, bdl-9, bdl-10, bdl-11 and a Saha subset) validates every outbound EHR and mock ABDM document before anything is sent, stamps it, and refuses a deliberate violation with a specific error; 14-case regression corpus. No NRCeS profile package or terminology validator is installed.
requirements.remaining: Pinned NRCeS profile package, HL7 validator, terminology and mapping bundle, owner-approved upgrades, and a partner-agreed regression corpus.

requirements.title: Health Information Provider operation
requirements.requirement: When operating as or through a HIP, the platform shall create eligible records, preserve care-context linkage, respond only through authorised exchange, encrypt and transmit the required payload, and retain the ABDM acknowledgement and failure state.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A consented request retrieves only the authorised records and produces traceable request, encryption, transfer, acknowledgement and error evidence without exposing unrelated records.
requirements.current: Slice 7b: care-context linking of confirmed visits under the current ABHA, and a mock HIP that encrypts consent-covered bundles for the requester (X25519, HKDF-SHA-256, AES-256-GCM) with checksums and delivery acknowledgement. Local mock gateway only.
requirements.remaining: Real gateway routing, partner HIP onboarding, ABDM-conformant encryption and callbacks, and more record types.

requirements.title: Health Information User operation
requirements.requirement: When operating as or through an HIU, the platform shall request the minimum health information needed for the approved purpose, track consent and data-flow states, validate received bundles, preserve external provenance and prevent silent overwriting of local records.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A received record is shown with its source and effective date, while invalid, duplicate or conflicting content enters the configured reconciliation path.
requirements.current: Slice 7b: consent-bound fetch with transfer tracking, decryption, checksum and bundle-type validation, and clinician review before any received record is accepted. Local mock gateway only.
requirements.remaining: Real consent-manager and gateway data flow, NRCeS profile validation and merging accepted records into care.

requirements.title: EHR connector capability profile
requirements.requirement: Every EHR or HMIS connector shall publish a capability profile covering supported resources or documents, search keys, read and write operations, authentication, patient matching, terminology, versioning, latency, idempotency, receipts, amendments, deletion restrictions and support ownership.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: The platform enables only operations declared in the active profile and blocks configuration that assumes unsupported search, update or acknowledgement behaviour.
requirements.current: Native FHIR capability profile gates document retrieval/publication.
requirements.remaining: Reference-partner profile covering all declared search/update/version/receipt/support behaviour.

requirements.title: EHR writeback and conflict handling
requirements.requirement: The platform shall preserve the EHR as authority for its accepted records and shall use destination-supported identifiers, conditional updates, versions or reconciliation before writeback. Conflicting updates shall not be resolved through last-write-wins unless the destination owner explicitly approves that rule for the record type.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Concurrent-update tests preserve both versions, prevent silent loss and route unresolved conflicts to the named operational owner.
requirements.current: Conditional document creation and duplicate receipt lookup. Slice 7f: a named reconciliation owner (owner or administrator) per EHR connection; publication conflicts (several documents, or a different one, under the publication's identifier with an authoritative search) hold the visit and appear in the exception queue for that owner, who is also named on unknown-outcome rows. Current human purpose/scope and bound service status/expiry/accountable ownership guard retrieved candidate intake and clinical staging; original conflicting documentary versions remain retained.
requirements.remaining: EHR updates/amendments, destination version conflicts and recording a conflict's resolution in Saha.

requirements.title: Legacy and document exchange
requirements.requirement: Where FHIR is unavailable, the platform may use authorised HL7 v2, CDA, REST, SOAP, file or document exchange. The connector shall label the resulting limitations, preserve the original artefact and avoid presenting batch preparation or document extraction as real-time structured acceptance.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A batch or document connector identifies its delay, source document, extracted fields, reviewer and destination receipt; unsupported writeback remains unavailable.
requirements.current: Reviewed FHIR document route preserves source and limitations.
requirements.remaining: Approved legacy HL7 v2/CDA/REST/SOAP/file adapters as selected by buyer.

requirements.title: Terminology and mapping governance
requirements.requirement: Clinical codes, local programme values, units and mapping tables shall be versioned, reviewed and tested for the specific source and destination. Unmapped, deprecated or ambiguous concepts shall not be silently replaced with the nearest available code.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A terminology change produces an impact report and blocks affected submissions until the mapping is approved or the value is explicitly represented as unmapped.
requirements.current: Small explicit LOINC/unit whitelist and mapping versions. App-first B07 source-versioned revisions can declare explicit partner-local/LOINC target codes and active/deprecated/ambiguous status; impact records declaration counts and refuses unresolved publication. These are owner declarations, not a terminology registry or clinical code approval. App-first reviewed conformance adds closed deterministic transform and unit/missing rules, explicit unmapped handling and independent source-versioned required-field/code examples; per-field impact protects current queued work and reviewed rollback preserves conformance.
requirements.remaining: Native partner/clinical terminology and source semantics acceptance, representative external conformance corpus and larger-history qualification remain. Closed deterministic software semantics and owner-declared conformance are delivered; they do not establish partner approval. Unknown delivery remains lookup-only.

requirements.title: Conformance and production claims
requirements.requirement: The platform shall distinguish syntactic validation, sandbox success, security review, partner certification, production onboarding and live operational acceptance. Marketing, administration and status screens shall not collapse these states into a single compliant label.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A sandbox-passing connector cannot be labelled production-live until credentials, owner approval, end-to-end transaction evidence and support responsibility are recorded.
requirements.current: UI and release gates distinguish simulation, configured endpoints and real acceptance.
requirements.remaining: Independent review of all production claims when onboarding evidence exists.

requirements.title: Defined offline capability
requirements.requirement: Previously authorised users shall be able to access a limited encrypted caseload, capture encounters, review valid cached guidance and prepare tasks during outages. Functions needing remote information or models shall show their unavailable or pending state.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: The core offline visit test completes without network access; no cloud model is falsely shown as having run.
requirements.current: Encrypted bounded draft notebook with unavailable online functions. Slice 3g: new people, first-visit facts and referral requests can be captured offline and wait in the encrypted notebook until sync. App-first A02 adds a public locked offline /app shell sharing the unchanged encrypted field vault: current prepared visits, capture and sync; account/packet-owner/lifetime gates, ciphertext-only storage and public-only caches; weight and notes survive actual offline browser reload. Synced visits remain unconfirmed until online review. The app view does not claim a full offline caseload or approved-guidance cache. App-only connected patient-scope revalidation and redirect refusal are independently browser-tested; prepared-visit scope remains narrower than a complete offline caseload. A05 adds signed prepared documentary task types and complete captured programme pack/version guidance, encrypted offline conditional answers and explicit absence reasons. New server-held work digests and captured episode/version checks apply before sync even if an older client omits its optional digest. Sync remains an unconfirmed draft; clinical approval remains pending.
requirements.remaining: Cached approved guidance, wider task capture and actual offline device acceptance.

requirements.title: Durable local capture
requirements.requirement: The application shall acknowledge a save only after local persistence succeeds. Insufficient storage, database failure or encryption failure shall be shown before the worker believes a record has been saved.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Forced restart and low-storage tests preserve acknowledged data or clearly report that saving did not complete.
requirements.current: Serialized encrypted writes acknowledge after persistence; recovery logic tested. App-first A02 adds a public locked offline /app shell sharing the unchanged encrypted field vault: current prepared visits, capture and sync; account/packet-owner/lifetime gates, ciphertext-only storage and public-only caches; weight and notes survive actual offline browser reload. Synced visits remain unconfirmed until online review. The app view does not claim a full offline caseload or approved-guidance cache. Both app/field surfaces preserve latest encrypted book during queued timing/access updates, with originating-account checks and fail-closed CAS. Explicit abandoned unsent links can be retired without deleting accepted/unknown request evidence.
requirements.remaining: Actual IndexedDB crash/restart/low-storage fault injection on supported physical devices and wider task recovery qualification.

requirements.title: Controlled offline authority
requirements.requirement: Offline access shall use a time-bounded grant with scoped data and actions. Default proposal: a 24-hour grant after online verification; extending it up to 72 hours requires deployment approval. New privileged grants and remote disclosures remain online-only.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Expired grants lock cached patient records. Operators understand that revocation cannot reach a disconnected device before reconnection or local expiry.
requirements.current: Signed 24-hour scoped grants, expiry and reconnect checks.
requirements.remaining: Managed keys/trusted device clock and approved deployment-specific extension policy.

requirements.title: Pending media and AI work
requirements.requirement: Recordings and images shall be queued with purpose, quality state and retention rules. On reconnection the platform shall recheck eligibility and authorisation before sending media to a provider.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An offline request is cancelled or routed for review when its permission expires or its capability is suspended before upload.
requirements.current: Slice 3a: field-notebook queue of photos and voice notes with purpose, local quality checks and device retention, sealed per item; on reconnection the grant, patient access and draft visit are rechecked before upload, and failures route items to review without sending. Slices 3d and 3e: voice notes recorded in the notebook; camera photos re-encoded on the device under the size limit without embedded location metadata.
requirements.remaining: Provider/capability revalidation once media is sent to a provider; clinical adequacy of reduced photos; background upload; real-device, low-storage and eviction testing.

requirements.title: Safe synchronisation ordering
requirements.requirement: Dependent records shall synchronise in a valid order, preserving identities and stable submission identifiers. The application shall recover from intermittent connectivity without replaying successful actions.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A new local person, encounter and referral synchronise without orphan records across repeated connection loss and restoration.
requirements.current: Stable-key sync for existing authorised person and visit drafts. Slice 3g: a person registered offline, with a first visit draft and referral request, is created in one command keyed by a stable registration id, so resends under new keys never create a second person; Sync all sends registrations, then visit drafts, then media, stops on an uncertain outcome and retries it with the same key; tested with repeated lost responses. Slice 3h: a clinician turns the synced request into a referral in one step, or declines it, once the visit is confirmed. Slice 3i: open synced requests are listed for clinicians and supervisors until decided.
requirements.remaining: Physical-device testing across real connection loss, and background sync.

requirements.title: Revalidation of delayed actions
requirements.requirement: Queued actions shall be revalidated against current assignment, permissions, patient linkage, protocol and input freshness before execution. A delayed clinical action shall not proceed solely because it was once drafted.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A material rule or data change places the action into review with an explanation instead of silently executing the old plan.
requirements.current: Assignment, identity, membership, consent and visit versions rechecked at sync. Slice 3a: queued media is uploaded only after the grant, patient access and draft visit are rechecked. A05 adds signed prepared documentary task types and complete captured programme pack/version guidance, encrypted offline conditional answers and explicit absence reasons. New server-held work digests and captured episode/version checks apply before sync even if an older client omits its optional digest. Sync remains an unconfirmed draft; clinical approval remains pending.
requirements.remaining: Protocol/freshness revalidation for expanded queued tasks, and provider revalidation for media.

requirements.title: Shared and lost devices
requirements.requirement: The application shall isolate local user data, hide sensitive notifications, support quick locking and allow remote revocation when connectivity returns. Local encryption and grant expiry shall protect offline data where remote wiping cannot be guaranteed.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A second user cannot view the first user's cached records, and a reported lost device loses server access on its next contact.
requirements.current: Encrypted per-user notebook, inactivity lock, grants and reconnect denial. App-first A02 adds a public locked offline /app shell sharing the unchanged encrypted field vault: current prepared visits, capture and sync; account/packet-owner/lifetime gates, ciphertext-only storage and public-only caches; weight and notes survive actual offline browser reload. Synced visits remain unconfirmed until online review. The app view does not claim a full offline caseload or approved-guidance cache. Reconnected app visits are redacted during current permission validation and lock on positive withdrawal or login redirect.
requirements.remaining: Main-workspace shared-device protection, native keystore/MDM and lost-device exercises.

requirements.title: Offline workflow capacity
requirements.requirement: The approved device profile shall support at least 200 structured encounters and the media allowance defined in Section 23 without silent eviction of unsynchronised work. Users shall see storage and pending upload status.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A capacity test reaches the agreed limit, warns before exhaustion and preserves every acknowledged record.
requirements.current: Notebook supported ten drafts; slice 3j raises this to 200 visit drafts, tested in a Node client harness with save, restart and ordered Sync all at 200; slice 3a adds up to four queued media items per draft and 1 MB per notebook, raised in slice 3k to 100 queued items and 25 MB per device; slice 3b requests persistent storage, shows usage and pauses new visits and media when space is low. Slice 3k: 200 server-prepared visit drafts plus 100 reduced photos and voice notes in headless Chromium against the built Worker, with the 201st draft and the 101st item refused and nothing lost, lock and unlock, and two page reloads mid-sync ending with each visit and item on the server once.
requirements.remaining: 200 encounters on a real device, device-measured thresholds and no-eviction acceptance.

requirements.title: Action ownership
requirements.requirement: Every referral, follow-up and exception shall have an accountable person or team, a due time where appropriate, a reason and a current state. Unassigned work shall enter a monitored queue.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: No active urgent task can exist without a visible responsible queue or assignee.
requirements.current: Follow-up/referral/outreach owners; R10 unavailable-owner queue and handover. Slice 4b: per-patient action plan shows each open item's owner or responsible queue and flags items without a current eligible owner; a care worker takes ownership of an unowned follow-up or referral, and a supervisor or owner of the patient's team reassigns them. Slice 4d: a clinician with current access or a steward of the patient's team records that one follow-up or referral waits on another open item of the same patient; the plan shows each waiting item's blocker with the blocker's owner state and status, and what each item holds back.
requirements.remaining: All clinical/integration exceptions, urgency policy and production monitoring coverage; queue notification; safety-case reassignment outside clinicians.

requirements.title: Service directory
requirements.requirement: Referral destinations shall come from an approved directory containing service capability, location, contact route, operating constraints and verification date. The agent shall not invent a facility or claim unverified availability.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A stale or unavailable service listing is labelled and routes the worker to an approved alternative or supervisor.
requirements.current: Versioned service metadata, contacts, constraints, verification and expiry gate source-backed referral drafts; legacy free text is labelled.
requirements.remaining: Real local-directory verification, urgent alternatives, availability updates and independent facility acceptance.

requirements.title: Referral lifecycle
requirements.requirement: The platform shall distinguish proposed, authorised, sent, received, scheduled, attended, completed, declined, cancelled and unknown outcomes where supported. A booked appointment or sent message shall not equal completed care.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Completion requires a defined evidence source and actor; unsupported closure attempts are rejected.
requirements.current: Dated referral events with evidence. SAHA-101 locally distinguishes proposed, authorised, sent, received, scheduled, attended and completed states; completion requires prior attendance, a coded service outcome, evidence source/reference and the recording actor. Declined, cancelled, not-attended and unknown dispositions remain distinct; closed states are immutable.
requirements.remaining: Facility-verified outcomes, partner integration, formal QA and observed external outcome evidence.

requirements.title: Due work and escalation
requirements.requirement: Workers and supervisors shall receive prioritised task lists based on approved urgency and due dates. Missed tasks shall escalate under programme rules while retaining the reason for delay and service constraints.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: An overdue case enters the correct supervisor queue and remains visible until completion or a documented resolution.
requirements.current: Versioned organisation-owned urgency and missed-outcome policy with explicit IANA timezone; no threshold is inferred before activation. Viewer-scoped worker priorities and supervisor/delegated-supervisor escalation cover open follow-ups and referrals, apply action-plan dependencies, retain current and prior patient ownership, due dates, reasoned delays and service constraints, and preserve source/audit history through completion or documented resolution. Follow-up delays pin patient, prior due date and policy versions and refuse changed scope, assignment, dependency or source. Nothing is sent and work is never reassigned automatically. See docs/current/SAHA-102-DUE-WORK-AND-ESCALATION.md.
requirements.remaining: Formal TC-BR-CARE-04-A/B, independent source review, exact-source CI, merge and observed deployment remain pending. Deployment-specific organisation/domain approval of thresholds and timezone, real recipient/on-call configuration and external notification delivery acceptance remain external gates.

requirements.title: Unified action plan
requirements.requirement: Actions arising from multiple programmes shall be consolidated where clinically and operationally appropriate, retaining individual reasons and dependencies. Duplicate reminders shall be suppressed without hiding genuinely different work.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Two packs generating the same approved referral create one referral with both source links and appropriate programme completion states.
requirements.current: Shared visit facts and duplicate patient/day reminder suppression. Slice 4b: one ordered per-patient action plan across programme follow-ups, referrals, protocol reviews, safety cases and outreach, each with its source; follow-ups with the same title, due date and owner from several programme episodes shown once with every source. Slice 4d: recorded, audited dependencies between one patient's follow-ups, referrals and protocol reviews (self, cycle, closed-item and cross-patient links refused; removal needs a reason and keeps the record); a referral links further visits, protocol evaluations and programme episodes of the same patient, each with its kind and time, shown in the referral view and the action plan; single-source referrals are unchanged. Slice 10f: a referral can be created from several programme packs at once (createProgrammeReferrals): programme episodes on one confirmed visit that raise the same need for the same facility share one referral that links each asking episode as a source (slice 4d) and records which packs asked; the action plan names the asking packs on the referral's sources. Slice 13d: the household view records one read-audit event per member shown.
requirements.remaining: No dependency is derived automatically; packs do not declare their own referral needs (the worker names the need and the server matches it), referrals made before slice 10f carry no need and are never merged, and the need catalogue is a local default; programme pack migration and installation; dependencies are not applied to reminders, the escalation queue or caseload counts.

requirements.title: Safe communication preferences
requirements.requirement: Contact method, language, timing and disclosure preferences shall be recorded. Shared phone ownership shall be treated explicitly; sensitive content shall not be placed in notifications or message previews by default.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: A patient requesting private contact receives no revealing automated message through a household contact number.
requirements.current: Per-person, purpose and channel contact preferences now retain bounded ordered before/after change history, explicit phone ownership, preferred language, local contact window, permission, private-contact choice and a disclosure limit. Reminder drafts bind an exact purpose and recheck that purpose/channel before review and synthetic execution. Shared-phone delivery is limited to the fixed neutral template when explicitly permitted; private or unknown ownership prevents notification disclosure and retains the private or in-person follow-up path. Preference changes cancel only pending work for the affected purpose. Current assignment, record version and care-coordination purpose authority are enforced. Focused local contract evidence passes; no provider was called and no patient was contacted.
requirements.remaining: Formal TC-BR-CARE-06-A/B execution, representative-worker/domain acceptance, reviewed Hindi copy, approved live channel/provider and observed deployment remain pending.

requirements.title: External messaging and scheduling
requirements.requirement: Approved SMS, IVR, messaging or appointment services may be integrated with authorisation, delivery evidence, opt-out handling and escalation. Channels require separate readiness checks and shall not expose provider credentials to the agent.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Delivery failure creates a retry or follow-up task and is not reported as patient acknowledgement.
requirements.current: Synthetic-only complete application path: independently staged and reviewed per-channel readiness; exact message approval binds the current person, assignment, contact, template and channel; provider delivery, opt-out, recovery and direct patient acknowledgement are distinct; delivery failure creates worker-owned bounded retry and follow-up; synthetic execution refuses production; no credentials or provider calls. Existing staff STOP simulation and exact-organisation signed mock callback preserve stable durable receipts, preference/consent history and unsent reminder cancellation.
requirements.remaining: Approved live SMS/IVR/messaging/appointment provider, server credentials, real incoming events or receipts, sender/channel/language qualification, formal TC-BR-CARE-07-A/B, independent final review, CI, merge and observed deployment remain pending.

requirements.title: Worker activity evidence
requirements.requirement: The system shall generate a reviewable record of verified worker activities for programme reporting or incentive support. It shall distinguish performed, claimed, verified and submitted activity and avoid promising payment.
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance: Correcting or cancelling an activity updates derived claims and leaves the original evidence and review history traceable.
requirements.current: Visit-backed outreach completion and correction-aware evidence. Slice 4c: per-worker summary for supervisors separating performed, claimed, verified (evidence-matched) and submitted activity, with corrections traced to reviser and reason and no payment language or location. Slice 10c: worker incentive claims on an owner-set synthetic placeholder schedule (not a real rate): an ASHA prepares a claim from her own current confirmed visits and outreach completions, each line linked to its source record and never claimed twice; the team supervisor verifies or returns it with a reason; a different owner approves; an approved claim is immutable and stored with a digest chained to the previous claim, with corrections as new linked claims and a CSV export carrying the digests; no payment is made or implied. requirements.title: Privacy-preserving aggregation
requirements.requirement: Reports shall enforce audience-specific aggregation and small-cell controls. Patient-level drilldown and exports shall require an approved purpose and separate access.

requirements.current: Current team scope and administrator patient-aggregate denial. Slice 6d indicator queries refuse cohorts under 5 and suppress small and complementary cells. Slice 6s adds per-definition minimum cohorts, differencing protection across one viewer's nested queries over seven days (hashed filters and per-cell people counts only, no patient data), and a CSV of indicator results that keeps the suppression; slice 6s-2 gives that CSV an export identifier, a row-count and SHA-256 manifest and an audit event. Slice 6w (fifth independent review): differencing compares numerators, denominators and denominator minus numerator as well as people; definition filters (sex, age band, programme) are nesting dimensions, so complementary definitions, including several in one query, are compared; the ledger is pruned by time only and refuses new queries at a per-viewer (400) or organisation (4,000) bound instead of evicting; a view moves no revision and writes no command receipt, queries are POST only, and data exit leaves the ledger out. Slice 6aa (seventh independent review): differencing is also checked through the people behind each release rather than by key: every measure release of the viewer's last seven days is re-evaluated against the people in scope now and split into atoms (people, and window-to-window increments for windowed measures, in exactly the same shown cells); a result that would create or split an atom of 1 to 4 is withheld, so a different grouping, an exclusion definition or a different window no longer bypasses it; the window is part of each release's identity; the ledger is bounded by size (1 MB organisation, 250 KB per viewer, 429 when full); a property test over random synthetic query sequences finds no released nested pair differing by 1 to 4; the remaining limits (two viewers combining results, changes between queries, releases older than seven days, unrelated measures) are stated to owners. Slice 6ad (ninth review): a release for a window that ended in the past records its end, used in the window key, the ledger prune identity and the population check, which counts each window to its own end and falls back to whole-person profiles when windows do not nest. Slice 13d: refused indicator queries (combination or cohort below 5) are recorded with filter names only and limited to 20 per viewer per day. App-first B27 protects frozen edition reads with current reporting purpose and entire original cohort scope, existing viewer disclosure guards, and durable comparison of actual contributions across previously disclosed editions; small changed groups are withheld and concurrent disclosure registration is guarded. Operational report export refuses raw units/disclosure state and resealed unsupported metadata/history; current cohort/purpose after-audit gates remain. This does not replace full protected reconstruction or full owner-expression privacy work. Composite privacy screening retains every primitive dependency and actual joint cohort membership profile, including zero contributors, across current/frozen and destination releases. Independent current-authority tests refuse late-audit reporting-purpose/programme withdrawal403 and supported clinical/definition changes409 without returning former figures. Existing cross-viewer/collusion and operating-policy residuals remain.
requirements.remaining: Differencing across viewers, non-nested filters, groupings and definitions, suppression on the operational export and other report paths, and a separate purpose for patient exports.
